answer: Each identity binds one recorded water right to one parcel: the registry checks it live, a meter proves use, and non-use forfeits it. A tundra parcel with a senior right costs $12,000; one season takes 365 days: one fake identity costs $12,000 plus 365 days. Each right sits under a one-way cipher keyed to its deed, so a forgery fails. Cheapest cheat: leasing a farmer's right for $1,500 a year, but the meter is on the farmer's land and the right is already bound there, so it yields only a duplicate. One hundred fakes cost $1,200,000 and 36,500 days, a ripple no sybil farm can absorb.
